title: For r>=s+2 and 0<q<1 with regular nonresonant parameters, the divergent r-phi-s series is q^k-Borel–Laplace summable off its forbidden spiral and has the explicit theta/hypergeometric connection formula (3.2)
author: Shunya Adachi
source_title: The q-Borel Sum of Divergent Basic Hypergeometric Series
difficulty_reason: The author must convert a genuinely divergent higher basic hypergeometric series into a meromorphic sum and justify the analytic growth needed for its discrete Laplace transform. The proof combines a Slater continuation with a uniform spiral-excluded theta-growth estimate and a nontrivial reorganization of the discrete Laplace sum into r convergent connection terms. This is an actual q-resummation/Stokes calculation beyond ordinary convergent hypergeometric identities or a formal Borel transform.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The full Theorem3.1 proof in Sections4–5 was read with the q-Borel/Laplace definitions and the exact parameter/domain conditions. The author computes the p=q^k Borel transform, supplies its Slater continuation, proves p-exponential growth uniformly off the forbidden q-spiral using the theta quasiperiodicity and a compact fundamental annulus, and evaluates the discrete Laplace sum by an explicit double-series reindexing. The established summability/Gevrey theorem and Slater connection formula are credited prior background; the needed growth proof and new p-Laplace computation are supplied here. The convergence domain of the resulting ordinary hypergeometric series is explicitly retained. No q->1 confluence or earlier disputed Morita formula is counted.

statement_scope: Exactly Theorem3.1 restricted to 0<q<1, integers r>=s+2 and k=r-s-1, p=q^k. All a_i,b_j are nonzero; b_j and a_i avoid {1,q^-1,q^-2,...} so denominators are regular and the starting series is nonterminating; a_i/a_j is not in q^Z for i!=j. For lambda not in (-1)^k q^Z, the p-Borel transform is p-exponentially controlled on its admissible spiral and the p-Laplace sum is given by (3.2) at x not in [-lambda;p] with |q*b_1*...*b_s/(a_1*...*a_r*x)|<1, furnishing the explicit continuation of its meromorphic summation germ. The at-most-simple poles are contained in [-lambda;p]. No parameter singularity continuation or q->1 limit is selected.
